title: Gas Prices Jump 44% as War with Iran Hits Your Wallet
summary: Have you noticed your family talking about higher prices at the gas station? You're not alone. The war between the U.S. and Iran has sent gasoline prices soaring. On Tuesday, the average price for a gallon of regular gas was over $4.50. That's about 44% more than it cost last year at this time! Why? Because Iran blocked a narrow waterway called the Strait of Hormuz. About one-fifth of the world's oil passes through there. When that oil can't get out, prices shoot up. The government said that overall prices in April were 3.8% higher than a year ago. That's the biggest jump in three years. Gasoline alone jumped 5.4% just from March to April. This is tough for many families. Heather Long, an economist, said inflation is now eating up all wage gains. That means even if people get raises, the higher prices cancel them out. People are cutting back on fun spending. One woman said she drives to work twice a day—it's only five minutes, but she feels the cost. For big shopping, she drives 40 minutes to a mall. The war started on February 28 when the U.S. and Israel attacked Iran. Now, the Federal Reserve, which controls interest rates, is being careful. It might not lower rates soon because of the war. President Trump wants lower rates, but the Fed is worried about inflation getting worse. It's a tricky situation, and many Americans are feeling the squeeze.
why_it_matters: If your family spends more on gas, there may be less money for fun outings, snacks, or activities, so it touches your daily life directly.

background_read: The Strait of Hormuz (a narrow sea passage between Iran and Oman) is one of the most important oil routes in the world. When conflicts block it, fuel prices can rise quickly everywhere.
The Federal Reserve (the U.S. central bank, often called 'the Fed') adjusts interest rates to keep the economy from overheating or slowing too much. If inflation is high, it may keep rates high.
The war between the U.S. and Iran (which started on February 28 after joint attacks) has disrupted global oil supplies and made many families nervous about rising costs.
